# Boardcall

> Boardcall is a native iOS app that turns raw swell, wind, and tide data into a plain-English daily surf briefing plus a board recommendation pulled from the surfer's own quiver — modeled by each board's real length, width, thickness, and volume, not a generic size guess.

Boardcall is not the first or only iOS app that recommends a board for conditions. See the guides below for how it's actually positioned relative to Surfline and to Surf Forecast: Quiver, the named competitor that already does per-spot board suggestions.

## Site

- [Boardcall — Surf Forecast App That Picks Your Board](https://boardcall.app/): the marketing homepage. Screenshots, a plain-English walkthrough of how the board pick is calculated, and an FAQ (also summarized below).

## App

- [Boardcall: Surf Briefing on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6798369030): free iOS app for iPhone and iPad, no account or login required. Every morning it reads swell, wind, and tide at the surfer's chosen spot and writes a plain-English briefing with a go/no-go verdict — fire, fun, marginal, or skip — plus a board pick from the boards the user has actually added, across 263 built-in surf spots worldwide.

## Key facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad), free to download.
- No account, login, signup, or password anywhere in the app; boards, spots, and profile are stored on-device, not in an account.
- 263 built-in surf spots worldwide: the full US coastline, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, a Great Lakes cluster, and 40+ countries internationally. No GPS or location tracking — the user picks from the built-in list.
- 258 real surfboard models in a built-in catalog, sourced from actual manufacturer dimensions and volumes, across longboard, mid-length, fish, groveler, shortboard, step-up, gun, and soft-top — or the user can enter their own board's exact dimensions.
- Board pick logic: a deterministic physics calculation (length × width × thickness → volume, adjusted for board shape, matched against wave face height, swell period, wind, skill level, and body weight) decides the recommended board. An AI model (Claude) can write the plain-English explanation of that pick, but the pick itself is never the AI's call.
- Briefings: a free, unlimited, deterministic (non-AI) plain-English briefing is available every day at no cost. Boardcall Pro ($6.99/mo or $54.99/yr) raises the weekly cap on richer AI-written briefing prose from 4/week to unlimited, and adds a weekly AI "coach" note on patterns from the user's own logged sessions. Nothing else is gated behind Pro.
- Safety gate: a beginner or intermediate surfer's daily verdict is automatically capped (it will never show "fire") when conditions exceed the skill level the user has entered.
- Data sources: wave and wind data from Open-Meteo; tide data from NOAA CO-OPS (US spots only — international and Great Lakes spots do not have tide data).
- Differentiator vs. plain surf-report/forecast apps (Surfline, generic marine-forecast apps): those report conditions and stop, leaving the surfer to decide; Boardcall closes the loop by naming the one specific board from the surfer's own quiver to bring, and why.

## FAQ

- **Is Boardcall free to use?** Yes — Boardcall is free to download, with unlimited daily briefings, the full board-pick engine across your whole quiver, the worldwide spot map, and the six-day forecast all included. Boardcall Pro ($6.99/mo or $54.99/yr) only raises the weekly cap on richer AI-written briefings from 4/week to unlimited and adds a weekly AI coaching note based on your own logged sessions.
- **Does Boardcall require an account or login?** No. There's no signup, login, or password — your boards, spots, and profile are stored on your device, not in an account.
- **How does Boardcall decide which surfboard to bring?** It calculates real volume for every board in your quiver from length × width × thickness (adjusted for shape), matches it against today's wave face height, period, and wind plus your skill level and body weight, and names the one board that fits best — an AI model then writes the plain-English explanation.
- **What surfboard volume do I need for my weight and skill level?** It depends on both — heavier and less experienced surfers generally need more volume — but wave size and period shift that target by another 10–45%, which is why a single fixed number is only a starting point.
- **Is Boardcall a good alternative to Surfline?** For checking conditions and getting a board recommendation, yes — Boardcall's free tier includes unlimited briefings, the full worldwide spot map, and board picks with no paywall, though it doesn't include Surfline's live surf-cam network.
- **What does "chest high" or "waist high" actually mean in feet?** Roughly: knee-to-waist is 2–3 ft face height, waist-to-chest is 3–4 ft, and chest-to-shoulder is 4–5 ft. Boardcall reports every forecast in these plain-English terms instead of a bare number.
- **Is it safe for a beginner to surf overhead waves?** Generally no — overhead waves (roughly 5 ft+ face height) call for real experience and strong paddle power. Boardcall's safety gate automatically caps that day's verdict and warns beginners when conditions exceed their stated skill level.
- **How cold does the water need to be before I need a wetsuit?** Most surfers want at least a spring suit below about 75°F and a full wetsuit well before 65°F, with real hypothermia risk climbing fast under 50°F. Boardcall reads actual water temperature at your spot and gives a direct wetsuit call.

## Guides

- [How Much Volume Does Your Surfboard Actually Need?](https://boardcall.app/blog/surfboard-volume-explained/): the real variables — body weight, skill level, swell period, and wave size — that determine correct board volume, explained independent of any app.
- [Why a Bigger Wave Needs a Bigger Board, Not a Smaller One](https://boardcall.app/blog/why-big-waves-need-more-volume/): the paddle-power mechanic behind why a step-up or gun carries more volume than an everyday shortboard, not less.
- [Which Surf Apps Actually Recommend a Board?](https://boardcall.app/blog/surf-apps-that-recommend-a-board/): an honest 2026 rundown of the iOS surf apps that ship a board-recommendation feature, and how they differ.
- [Boardcall vs. Surfline vs. Surf Forecast: Quiver](https://boardcall.app/blog/boardcall-vs-surfline-vs-quiver/): a direct, three-way comparison of what each app actually does differently.
- [Fire, Fun, Marginal, Skip: Why Boardcall Answers in a Verdict](https://boardcall.app/blog/surf-forecast-verdict-fire-fun-marginal-skip/): why the app returns a capped, plain-language verdict instead of a raw numeric score.
- [What a Surfboard Recommendation App Should Actually Do](https://boardcall.app/guides/surfboard-recommendation-app.html): what separates a real board-matching engine from a one-time buying quiz.
- [Which Surfboard Should I Ride Today?](https://boardcall.app/guides/which-surfboard-should-i-ride-today.html): the actual decision framework — wave face, period, wind, and board volume — surfers use to pick a board for a given day.
- [Surfboard Volume Chart by Weight and Skill Level](https://boardcall.app/guides/surfboard-volume-chart-by-weight-and-skill-level.html): a practical volume lookup by body weight and skill level, and how wave size/period shift the target.
- [Signs Your Surfboard Has the Wrong Volume](https://boardcall.app/guides/signs-your-surfboard-has-wrong-volume.html): the diagnostic signs a board is over- or under-volumed for the surfer riding it.
- [Is It Safe for a Beginner to Surf Overhead Waves?](https://boardcall.app/guides/is-it-safe-for-beginners-to-surf-overhead-waves.html): real risk factors and skill thresholds for overhead surf.
- [How Do I Know If the Waves Are Too Big for Me?](https://boardcall.app/guides/how-do-i-know-if-the-waves-are-too-big-for-me.html): a practical framework for judging whether conditions exceed your own level.
- [Wave Height Guide: Feet to Body Parts](https://boardcall.app/guides/wave-height-guide-feet-to-body-parts.html): the standard surf-size vocabulary (ankle high through double overhead) mapped to real face-height feet.
- [Surf Forecast App With No Account Required](https://boardcall.app/guides/surf-forecast-app-no-account.html): what data an accountless surf app actually stores, and what Boardcall specifically keeps on-device vs. sends to a server.
- [Free Surfline Alternative: What You Actually Get for $0](https://boardcall.app/guides/free-surfline-alternative.html): a feature-by-feature breakdown of what Surfline paywalls vs. what's genuinely free, including in Boardcall.
- [How Cold Is Too Cold to Surf Without a Wetsuit?](https://boardcall.app/guides/how-cold-is-too-cold-to-surf-without-a-wetsuit.html): real water-temperature-to-wetsuit-thickness thresholds and hypothermia risk signs.
